content.text: I couldn't open the repository, and the retrieved snippets don't include the session-deletion code. This diagnosis is inferred from the call graph and the bug description, so the line ranges are approximate.

candidates.explanation: On a password change, update() calls sessionService.deleteByUserIdWithExclude to end the user's other sessions. The exclusion is likely wrong. It probably passes the wrong identifier (for example the user id, or a value that doesn't match the session id type) as excludeSessionId, instead of userJwtPayload.sessionId. The current session is then not excluded and gets deleted, so the next refresh-token call returns 401.

The exclusion filter may be wrong here. It may use a plain equality or type-mismatched comparison where it needs Not(excludeId). In that case the current session is deleted and another session is kept. The same logic exists in the document (Mongo) repository, which may use $eq instead of $ne or compare ids with the wrong type.

This service wrapper forwards the parameters to the repository. If it maps userId or excludeSessionId incorrectly, for example by swapping them or dropping the exclusion, the current session is not preserved.

fix.description: In AuthService.update, after a successful password change, call sessionService.deleteByUserIdWithExclude({ userId: currentUser.id, excludeSessionId: userJwtPayload.sessionId }). Make sure the exclusion uses the current session id from the JWT payload and has the same type as the stored id. In the repository, delete rows where user matches and id is not the excluded id (Not(excludeSessionId) in relational, $ne in Mongo).
